messages:
Alex T.: taking primary for the US-EAST->EU overlap window (next 8h). I'm stepping in after Jon. primary=Alex, secondary=Maria. quick note: we still have that intermittent kv-cache spike from yesterday, watch for >95th latency.
IncidentBot: Pager triggered (kv-cache-high-latency) — 1:03 UTC — alert ID: alert-kv-4433 — severity: P2 — routed to eng-oncall.
Maria K.: ack. I'm secondary; reachable via DM and pager. any fresh customer impact?
Alex T.: no new escalations in the last hour. calling out two quick remediation pointers in the runbook that were handy yesterday: 1) roll partial KV cache snapshot fallback 2) scale dedicated worker pool by +2.
Jon P.: fyi the canary for the cache-ttl-change is still rolling in us-east-1, might be correlated. if latency > 300ms then abort canary (see runbook).
Maya R.: re: abort canary — run these steps if we need to kill the rollout quickly:
```
# abort canary
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $SRE_TOKEN" \
  https://deploy.redwood.internal/api/v1/rollouts/abort -d '{"rollout_id":"canary-cache-ttl-2026-03"}'
# scale pool manually
kubectl -n inference scale deploy/kv-worker --replicas=6
```
Alex T.: quick checklist I'm leaving in the handoff: monitor dashboards + alertset, keep ephemeral traces for any 5xxs, check prefix-cache hit rate. links: https://console.redwood/runbooks/kv-cache-fallback and https://console.redwood/dashboards/kv-latency
SRE Rotation: note — small coverage gap from 02:00–02:45 UTC where Maria is on a meeting; Alex pls escalate to the oncall lead if you need an extra hand.
Maria K.: thanks. I'm free at 02:45. if we need immediate mitigation during meeting, tag @Maya R. (she's near infra). Also toggling the feature-flag for cache-ttl is an option: https://flags.redwood/internal/flag/cache-ttl-change
Jon P.: adding two quick remediation bullets to the thread so they're visible during handoff:
- If >1% 5xx: set fallback=true in kv-proxy config (instant fallback, temp perf hit but restores stability).
- If tail-latency persists and scaling doesn't help: roll back canary -> use previous artifact id: artifact-20260302-07
Maya R.: small diagnostic commands I run when I jump in:
```
# tail error logs for kv proxy
kubectl -n inference logs -l app=kv-proxy -f --tail=200 | grep -i "error\|timeout"
# check redis connection pool stats
redis-cli -h kv-proxy-svc info | egrep "connected_clients|blocked_clients|used_memory_human"
```
Alex T.: adding runbook snippets inline for quicker copy/paste:
- quick restart (use only if one host misbehaving): `systemctl restart redwood-kv-worker` on that host or `kubectl rollout restart deploy/kv-worker -n inference`
- toggle fallback via configmap:
```
kubectl -n inference patch configmap kv-proxy-config -p '{"data":{"fallback":"true"}}'
kubectl -n inference rollout restart deploy/kv-proxy
```
IncidentBot: Deployment canary observed increased 5xx rate at 01:57 UTC. Related alerts: alert-kv-4433, alert-deploy-912.
Alex T.: plan for the shift: 1) I keep primary pager until 03:00 UTC. 2) Maria is primary from 03:00–07:00 UTC. 3) If we hit P1 (widespread customer impact) page all-hands via incident channel and run the major incident playbook (link: https://console.redwood/playbooks/major-incident).
Maria K.: got it. I'll watch the 'kv tail latency' panel and the 95th token latency. If anything, I'll escalate to infra oncall.
Jon P.: leaving one small note from yesterday's postmortem: if you see KV cache TTL skew between regions, run the TTL sync job: `python tools/sync_kv_ttl.py --region us-east-1` — it fixed a similar outage.
Maya R.: thumbs up. I'll be on-call-standby for 30m in case you need hands to run the rollback.
Alex T.: final: logging the runbook quick links here so they're top-level in thread: [Runbook: KV cache fallback] https://console.redwood/runbooks/kv-cache-fallback, [Rollback guide] https://console.redwood/runbooks/rollback, [Major incident playbook] https://console.redwood/playbooks/major-incident. keep this thread for the handoff notes.
Maria K.: copied. ping me for any hotfixes; I'll jump in. :thumbsup:
